value.title: RCE via OOM corruption

items.wording: unconditionally invokes the request shutdown procedure
items.quote: Apache mod_php unconditionally invokes the request shutdown procedure, even when request startup has failed.

items.wording: susceptible, though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated
items.quote: Source analysis therefore supports FPM as a susceptible, though no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI.
Source analysis indicates that FrankenPHP, analogous to Apache mod_php, calls the request shutdown procedure unconditionally, making it likely susceptible to application-independent attacks.

items.wording: application-specific exploits being likely but unvalidated
items.quote: LSAPI models FPM, with application-specific exploits being likely but unvalidated.
For installations that cannot update, setting and enforcing memory_limit=-1 administratively is the primary configuration mitigation.
Updating to a PHP release containing the patch to this vulnerability is the only complete mitigation.
This is not a complete mitigation.
Keep post_max_size conservative and independently enforce the decoded request size at the frontend.
Reduce max_input_nesting_level, and bound the number of input variables, multipart parts, headers within each part and uploads.
Do not use RLIMIT_AS or RLIMIT_DATA, as these will cause mmap() to fail once the memory limit is reached, triggering the vulnerable longjmp() path.
